card.name: Comma after eye-contact warnings
card.fires_on: The comma (or an adverb like 'immediately') ending an 'if eye contact occurs' or 'in case of contact' clause in topical product warnings, right before the instruction to rinse or wash.

modes.label: Comma after contact clause
modes.description: The comma closing an 'if/in case of contact' clause, just before 'rinse' or 'wash'.
modes.example: In case of contact<<,>> rinse thoroughly with water.

modes.label: Adverb before wash
modes.description: The word 'immediately' sits where the rinse instruction begins.
modes.example: Advise patients that if eye contact occurs,<< immediately>> wash out the eye with water or saline

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward rinse or wash (including Chinese equivalents) and away from unrelated tokens.
card.plain: It fires where a label says what to do after the product gets in the eyes, just before 'rinse with water'.
